why: A fourth sample of the same configuration, seed 4, and deliberately not a new experiment. ci-88, ci-90 and ci-91 ran lambda 0.9 with the ADR 0048 baseline on dataset seeds 1, 2 and 3, changing nothing else, and the value policy scored 0.6625, 0.0975 and 0.30375 against search-4. A 56-point spread from the seed alone is larger than every effect this project has measured, and each of those effects was measured one seed against one seed -- so ci-88 beating search-4 is inside the spread and is not a result, and neither is ADR 0048's 19-point win-rate gain, whose held-out fit improvement is real but whose win rate was a seed-1 sample. ADR 0049 proposes the fix: run a configuration on at least three seeds, report a spread, and have the gate require every seed. Until that lands, the loop still fires on every push, so this turn spends the slot widening the sample rather than making a new claim. The clone rows are the other lesson: ci-91's clone beats Greedy 0.82125, better than anything the loop has produced, and loses to the committed champion ci-69 at 0.42375 with an interval from 0.387, where ci-69 beats Greedy only 0.725. Being better against a third party does not make you better than the player you are replacing, and the champion bar refused it. What to read here: the value policy's numbers against Greedy and search-4 as a fourth point of the spread, not as a result on their own, and whether the clone against Greedy lands near seeds 2 and 3 (0.79875, 0.82125) or near seed 1 (0.725). Do not commit anything on a seed chosen for its score -- the benchmark seeds are fixed, so that is selection on the test set.
